provenance.instrument: South Fayette Township Code Chapter 240 Zoning (South Fayette Township Zoning Ordinance, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2026-01-14 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 4-2026 (2026-09-09), 'Zoning Amendment', Chapter 240, PDF only, not read. The residential use lists were last amended by Ord. No. 1-2025 and 2-2025 (2025).
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2026-01-14'. Ord. No. 4-2026 (zoning amendment, adopted 2026-09-09) is a New Law, not yet in the code text.
provenance.code_caution: Ord. No. 4-2026, a zoning amendment adopted 2026-09-09, is a New Law for Chapter 240 not yet in the code text (PDF, not opened). Its search excerpt amends the R-1 single-family lot width ('Single-family dwelling. b. With public sewers: 110 feet 125 feet', so 110 ft may now be 125 ft) and changes the zoning map (a Sturgeon zoning map change). The code search, which also covers New Laws text, found no accessory dwelling, accessory apartment or in-law wording in it.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment, in-law, ECHO or similar rule. Each residential district says 'only the following uses are authorized' (240-15, 240-22, 240-29, 240-36). In R-1 to R-4 and the Washington Pike Overlay 'any use not specifically listed as an authorized use in the zoning district shall not be permitted' (240-13A), and where single- or two-family dwellings are authorized 'the single-family dwelling or two-family dwelling shall be the only principal structure on the lot' (240-13C)

Side yards for a house: R-1 with public sewers 40 ft total, 10 ft minimum on one side (20 ft each side without sewers). R-2 25 ft total, 10 ft on one side (35 ft total, 15 ft on one side without sewers). R-3 10 ft each side. R-4 15 ft total, 5 ft on one side (30 ft total, 15 ft on one side without sewers) (240-16F, 240-23F, 240-30F, 240-37F)

A single-family dwelling is 'A detached residential building which is the only principal structure on the lot, designed exclusively for occupancy by one family ... and containing one dwelling unit' (240-9, dwelling types A). A second unit makes the building a two-family dwelling, which only R-4 (and the ND district) permits
R-4: two-family dwellings are permitted by right. Lot 12,000 sq ft with public sewers, 43,560 sq ft without, width 60 ft (150 ft without sewers) (240-36A(1)(c), 240-37)

Detached garages and storage buildings: not in the minimum front yard, 10 ft from side and rear lines (15 ft over 900 sq ft) in R-1 to R-3, 5 ft in R-4, 10 ft from the house. All accessory structures together at most 900 sq ft on a lot up to 20,000 sq ft, 1,000 sq ft up to 40,000, 1,200 sq ft up to 5 acres (240-99C(9), (11)). One story and 20 ft in R-1 and R-2, 15 ft in R-3 and R-4 (240-16I, 240-23I, 240-30I, 240-37I)
'Maximum lot coverage' counts all principal and accessory structures on the lot (240-99C(9)(b))

ND Neighborhood Design District: two-family dwellings are permitted by right, and 'More than one principal use or structure shall be permitted to occupy the same lot' (240-76.19A(1)(d)), 4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, but only within an approved neighborhood design development of at least 50 contiguous acres with public water and sewer (240-76.18, 240-76.20A(1), B(1)). Accessory residential buildings may have habitable space above the ground floor (20 ft high), but no accessory dwelling is listed (240-76.20L(1)(e))

C-1, C-2, PED, I-P and I-1: a use not listed may be authorized by the Zoning Hearing Board as a special exception for comparable uses (240-13B, 240-95A(13)). Those districts' use lists were not read. R-4 lists 'Apartment in combination with business' as a conditional use (240-36B(1)(a)), which is not an added unit for a house
provenance.notes: Zoning office: South Fayette Township Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (SO0208) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'family dwelling', relative, relatives, 'housekeeping unit', caretaker, 'guest house', 'accessory living', 'tenant house', 'accessory residential', conversion and duplex found no ADU text. The hits were the dwelling type definitions, area and bulk sections, the ND accessory residential building height, and the subdivision chapter's exclusion of a conversion into not more than three units from land development (215-8A). Read in full: Articles IV to VII (R-1 to R-4) and 240-99C. Read for its use list and accessory items: Article XIIC (ND). Not read: commercial, industrial, CD-1, B-1 and PED use lists, the Washington Pike Overlay beyond its use list (240-78), Article XIV open space design option, Article XV express standards (240-95, including (13) comparable uses and (45) Washington Pike Overlay conversion of dwelling), parking (Article XVII), the definition of lot coverage itself, Ord. No. 4-2026 (PDF). Fix round 2026-11-14 after an independent review, read again in the code: side yards stored as a total with the one-side minimum, Ord. No. 4-2026 excerpt noted, ND two-family path added, 240-13A to C cited, the Washington Pike Overlay use list read.

term.note: No ADU term. Searched for accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, family dwelling, relative, housekeeping unit, caretaker, guest house, accessory living, tenant house, accessory residential, conversion and duplex.

status.note: Each residential district lists the only uses authorized: single-family dwellings (and two-family dwellings in R-4) with customary accessory uses. No accessory dwelling unit. In R-1 to R-4 and the Washington Pike Overlay unlisted uses 'shall not be permitted' (240-13A), and a single- or two-family dwelling 'shall be the only principal structure on the lot' (240-13C).

path.note: Only the listed uses are authorized, and unlisted uses 'shall not be permitted' in R-1 to R-4 and the Washington Pike Overlay (240-13A). A house with a second unit is a two-family dwelling, which R-1, R-2 and R-3 do not list, so a second unit there needs a use variance. A second dwelling in a separate building is barred by 240-13C (the dwelling 'shall be the only principal structure on the lot'). In R-4 a two-family dwelling is permitted (see the other ways to add a unit).

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. The chapter article on the Board was not read.

unlisted_use_path.note: In C-1, C-2, PED, I-P and I-1 a use not listed may be authorized by the Zoning Hearing Board as a special exception under the standards for comparable uses not specifically listed. Their use lists were not read, so whether they list single-family or two-family dwellings is not known. Where a district lists a two-family dwelling, a second unit is read as that use, not an unlisted one.

value.name: Two-family dwelling in R-4
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling is a permitted principal use. Lot 12,000 sq ft with public sewers (43,560 without), width 60 ft (150 ft without), front 25 ft, rear 30 ft, lot coverage 35%, 45 ft.
value.note: Two dwelling units in one building ('including double houses and duplexes', 240-9). Converting an existing house into a two-family dwelling is read as this use. Not an ADU listing.

value.name: Two-family dwelling in a neighborhood design development (ND)
value.conditions: Two-family dwellings are permitted by right only as part of and within an approved neighborhood design development: a site of at least 50 contiguous acres, public water and public sewer, a mix of dwelling types. 4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, width 40 ft per unit, front 5 ft, side 5 ft, rear 20 ft (5 ft on an alley), 30 ft. More than one principal use or structure may occupy the same lot (240-76.19A(1)(d)).

requires.condition: The neighborhood design development site is at least 50 contiguous acres

value.note: Lot figure is two units at 4,000 sq ft each. A planned development approved through land development plans, not a path for adding a unit to one existing house outside such a development.
